evidence.quote: Call for non-EU students: 7 January 2027 – 7 March 2027
Only for NON-EU applicants residing outside Italy.
Save changes University of Padua My wishlist 0 Italy Sign in / register
• Valid Passport/Valid ID card (only for EU – or equivalent – applicants);
• Upper secondary school certificate/Academic qualification (if already obtained)
If your documents are issued only in a language other that Italian OR English, you will have to upload them together with official translations in Italian OR in English.
Language requirements English B2 Level (CEFR) or equivalent.
To be eligible for admission to a bachelor’s or a single-cycle degree, you need a minimum 12-year school record.

note.fr: Un test d'admission CISIA CEnT-S est requis ; inscrivez-vous sur le site CISIA et payez 55 €. Dates du premier macro-period : 26 nov. 2026, 17 déc. 2026.
note.en: A CISIA CEnT-S admission test is required; register on the CISIA website and pay €55. First macro-period dates: 26 Nov 2026, 17 Dec 2026.

evidence.quote: This degree programme requires the new CISIA CEnT-S test.

notes: Tuition left out: the programme page gives €2,950 per year, but the university page and the bando give a fixed non-EU fee of €2,990 (Group B) for students with non-EU citizenship and household not resident in Italy; no quote ties this programme to Group B, and the tie quote is missing (Bando Contribuzione has no such tasso for non-EU on page 3; page 5 tied only inferred from Group B general), hence no accepted tuition figure. Application channel: apply.unipd.it (university's own application portal, DreamApply) used for this programme; no Universitaly/preiscrizione quote found. More rounds exist (EU call 9 March 2027 – 9 April 2027); the first non-EU round was used (7 Jan 2027 – 7 March 2027). Deadline to graduate: 31 July 2027 (general). The programme page states CISIA CEnT-S test dates on 26 November 2026 and 17 December 2026. Entry qualification documents (diploma) accepted in English/Italian; official translations required if issued in another language; no legalised documents at application stage. The 'Valid Passport/Valid ID card' quote says 'only for EU – or equivalent – applicants', so for a Moroccan applicant this document is likely not applicable.
